observations.title: How the aerial survey defined the damage envelope
observations.locator: Section 2, printed page 1751 (PDF page 3), survey methods and Figure 1. Printed page 1752 (PDF page 4), EF0 width qualification and Figure 2.
observations.account: Wakimoto and colleagues combined June 1 and 3, 2013 ground surveys with a June 4 aerial survey. A Cessna 172 flew at 300 and 1200 m above ground and captured 1249 photographs. Where assessments differed, the ground estimate determined the assigned EF value. Their EF0 damage envelope reached roughly 7 km just east of Highway 81. They explicitly separate that envelope from the El Reno tornado alone: a separate anticyclonic tornado extended damage southeast, and the southern edge suggests rear-flank downdraft damage.
observations.limits: The roughly 7 km envelope does not replace the NWS 2.6-mile (about 4.2 km) maximum tornado width or final EF3 damage rating. Atlas links the paper without reproducing its figures. These survey methods establish no new Atlas coordinates, synchronized footage or registered appearance.

media.title: Historical NWRT reflectivity at source label 23:01:37
media.account: Historical NWRT phased-array reflectivity, in dBZ. The abrupt echo edge is present in the original published image, not an Atlas crop. NWRT could scan a limited azimuth sector, but this image alone does not establish the exact sampled footprint or the cause of every empty pixel. An unobserved area is not an observation of no rain. The full legend and printed source label are retained. Only a preceding frame up to four minutes old is shown. This regional product is not a georegistered overlay or a surface wind measurement.
media.limits: Times are transcribed from the filename printed inside each radar frame and interpreted as UTC, consistent with the NWS event chronology. The printed label does not itself state a time zone; this clock interpretation is explicit, not an independent calibration.

media.title: Roof loss while most walls remained standing
media.locator: Damage Photos, photograph 4, near Rother Road and SW 15th Street.
media.account: The original NWS caption assigns EF2 to this house: large sections of its roof were removed while most walls remained standing.
media.limits: That rating belongs to this damage example. The image alone does not establish wind speed, complete construction details or failure order. The nearby Photo 3 is another house, not an earlier or later view of this one. Exact camera coordinates and capture time remain unregistered.
